findings.title: Every running service is in the asset inventory
findings.action: Add every running service to the asset inventory
findings.why: Unknown services go unpatched and unmonitored.

findings.title: Backup copies are encrypted
findings.action: Encrypt the backups
findings.why: Unencrypted backups hand a full copy of the data to anyone who reaches the backup storage, bypassing every access control on the live systems.

findings.message: Plan mentions every reporting stage and the CSIRT
findings.title: Incident response plan covers the NIS2 reporting stages
findings.action: Add the NIS2 reporting deadlines and the CSIRT contact to the incident plan
findings.why: Missing a reporting deadline is itself a breach of Art. 23, separate from the incident.

assets.message: Plan mentions every reporting stage and the CSIRT

findings.title: Incident response plan has been reviewed recently
findings.action: Review the incident response plan and record the review date
findings.why: A stale plan lists wrong contacts and outdated systems when it is needed.

findings.message: All 2 accounts have or must enrol MFA
findings.title: Every staff account has MFA enrolled or is forced to enrol
findings.action: Turn on two-factor login for every account
findings.why: Staff accounts reach customer systems; a stolen password alone must not be enough.

assets.message: All 2 accounts have or must enrol MFA

findings.title: Accounts are locked after repeated failed logins
findings.action: Turn on protection against password guessing
findings.why: Limits online password guessing against staff accounts.

findings.title: Password policy enforces the profile's minimum length
findings.action: Set a minimum password length
findings.why: Short passwords weaken the first factor even when MFA is in place.

findings.title: Default admin credentials are rejected
findings.action: Change the default admin password
findings.why: Default admin credentials give anyone full control of every staff identity.

findings.title: Central logs are kept at least as long as the profile requires
findings.action: Keep logs for as long as the policy requires
findings.why: Logs deleted too early make an incident impossible to investigate or report.

findings.title: Central logs are kept at least as long as the profile requires
findings.action: Keep logs for as long as the policy requires
findings.why: Logs deleted too early make an incident impossible to investigate or report.

findings.title: SSH does not offer password authentication
findings.action: Allow only key-based server logins, not passwords
findings.why: Password logins on an admin host can be brute-forced or phished.

findings.title: Direct root login over SSH is disabled
findings.action: Stop direct administrator (root) logins to the server
findings.why: Shared root logins remove individual accountability and give an attacker full control.

findings.title: SSH limits authentication attempts per connection
findings.action: Limit login attempts per connection to the server
findings.why: Slows guessing, but is a minor control compared with key-only auth.

findings.title: TLS versions below the profile minimum are refused
findings.action: Switch off outdated encryption versions on the website
findings.why: Legacy TLS allows downgrade attacks on traffic to a public service.

findings.title: Certificate is valid and not about to expire
findings.action: Renew the website's certificate
findings.why: An invalid certificate trains users to click through warnings, which makes interception easier.

findings.message: HTTP redirects to HTTPS and HSTS is set
findings.title: Plain HTTP redirects to HTTPS and HSTS is set
findings.action: Send all website traffic over HTTPS
findings.why: Without a redirect and HSTS, users can be kept on unencrypted HTTP.

assets.message: HTTP redirects to HTTPS and HSTS is set

findings.title: No unaccepted, fixable vulnerability at the failing severity in running images
findings.action: Update software that has known critical flaws
findings.why: Known, fixable critical vulnerabilities are the most common way in.

not_assessed.title: Annual and event-driven policy review by management
not_assessed.quote: The network and information system security policy shall be reviewed and, where appropriate, updated by management bodies at least annually and when significant incidents or significant changes to operations or risks occur.

not_assessed.title: Documentation of review results
not_assessed.quote: The result of the reviews shall be documented.

not_assessed.title: Assign and revoke access rights on principles
not_assessed.quote: assign and revoke access rights based on the principles of need-to-know, least privilege and separation of duties

not_assessed.title: Modify access rights on employment change
not_assessed.quote: ensure that access rights are modified accordingly upon termination or change of employment
not_assessed.reason: organisational requirement: needs audit, not automated checks

not_assessed.title: Authorisation of access by relevant persons
not_assessed.quote: ensure that access to network and information systems is authorised by the relevant persons
not_assessed.reason: organisational requirement: needs audit, not automated checks

not_assessed.title: Control third-party access rights
not_assessed.quote: ensure that access rights appropriately address third-party access, such as visitors, suppliers and service providers, in particular by limiting access rights in scope and in duration

not_assessed.title: Maintain register of granted access rights
not_assessed.quote: maintain a register of access rights granted

not_assessed.title: Log access rights management
not_assessed.quote: apply logging to the management of access rights

not_assessed.title: Dedicated system administration accounts
not_assessed.quote: set up specific accounts to be used for system administration operations exclusively, such as installation, configuration, management or maintenance;

not_assessed.title: Administration accounts limited to administration systems
not_assessed.quote: provide that system administration accounts are only used to connect to system administration systems.

not_assessed.title: Controlled allocation of secret authentication information
not_assessed.quote: control the allocation to users and management of secret authentication information by a process that ensures the confidentiality of the information, including advising personnel on appropriate handling of authentication information

not_assessed.title: Termination of inactive sessions
not_assessed.quote: terminate inactive sessions after a predefined period of inactivity

not_assessed.title: Establish backup plans
not_assessed.quote: Based on the results of the risk assessment carried out pursuant to point 2.1 and the business continuity plan, the relevant entities shall lay down backup plans which include the following:

not_assessed.title: Recovery times in backup plans
not_assessed.quote: (a) recovery times;

not_assessed.title: Completeness and accuracy of backups
not_assessed.quote: (b) assurance that backup copies are complete and accurate, including configuration data and data stored in cloud computing service environment;

not_assessed.title: Safe offsite storage of backups
not_assessed.quote: (c) storing backup copies (online or offline) in a safe location or locations, which are not in the same network as the system, and are at sufficient distance to escape any damage from a disaster at the main site;

not_assessed.title: Restoring data from backups
not_assessed.quote: (e) restoring data from backup copies;

not_assessed.title: Backup retention periods
not_assessed.quote: (f) retention periods based on business and regulatory requirements.

not_assessed.title: Regular backup integrity checks
not_assessed.quote: The relevant entities shall perform regular integrity checks on the backup copies.
